source.title: ScAn-Bench: Evaluating Scaling Analysis Methodology
source.authors: Artin Sermaxhaj; Nastaran Alipour; Donat Sinani; Johannes Hog; Neeratyoy Mallik; Steven Adriaensen; J. Jitsev; Daniel Stoll

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates scaling-law loss and model-size extrapolation using surrogate benchmarks rather than reproducing the original large-scale training experiments. It measures how well these methods predict empirical outcomes under varied acquisition strategies and model families.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates loss extrapolation and compute-optimal model-size prediction on LLM and vision-language benchmarks. It also reports actual losses at extrapolated full configurations. It does not report downstream task scaling results for the scaling-law evaluation; those are explicitly excluded from the analysis. Surrogate prediction scores and acquisition-only metrics that do not measure the claim's scaling or extrapolation behavior are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits Kaplan-style power laws, Chinchilla Approach 3 and power-law N*(C) fits on runs below Cmax. It scores their predictions of minimal loss and optimal model size at 20×Cmax (and 10×) on LLM and CLIP benchmarks. This bears on V2, V3 and V7, and on V1 and V5 within a narrow range. Caveat: the 'empirical' targets come from TabPFN surrogates fitted to about 1,000 real runs per family, not from fresh training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that scaling-analysis outcomes are sensitive to acquisition and extrapolation choices and that no combination is best across benchmarks. They also conclude that Chinchilla3 fits loss well but predicts N* poorly when identifiability is weak or 6ND fails, and that power-law N* fits need acquisition that traces the compute-optimal frontier. They caveat small compute scales and possible non-transfer across pipelines.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks Kaplan-style and Chinchilla-style extrapolation approaches on surrogate representations of LLM and OpenCLIP training runs, rather than reproducing the original large-scale training studies. It also adapts acquisition baselines to use standardized, heuristic-free choices.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction outcomes vary with acquisition strategy (Iso-Parameter, Iso-FLOP, CARBS, Random Search), benchmark family (LLM versus OpenCLIP), and extrapolation method (Kaplan, Chinchilla Approach 3, empirical power-law fit). Full-configuration predictions are sensitive to the composition of the empirical Pareto frontier.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-parameter extrapolation by independent per-hyperparameter linear regression yields configurations with losses well above the best (e.g. CLIP 1.81–2.92 vs 0.41; LLM 1.71–2.02 vs 1.31).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Naive independent linear extrapolation of full hyperparameter configurations from small-scale Pareto points does not reach the compute-optimal loss at the target scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Data acquisition trade-off (Fig 1): CARBS has the lowest PER, A1 the highest hypervolume, and RS overtakes CARBS on incumbent loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Acquisition strategy for scaling-law data trades frontier accuracy against coverage.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026, Track on Evaluations and Datasets
record.problems: The authors state that the tested compute scales are substantially smaller than current state-of-the-art models, so trends may not transfer to larger regimes. Results do not always align across the LLM and VLM pipelines. Some findings are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. The paper also states that RS predictions monotonically improve with more data, although the LLM Table 4 values are 1.71 at 0.1×Ctarget and 1.89 at 0.5×Ctarget.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed trajectory and relative-ranking figures in Figures 7–19, including 10× target-scale plots and surrogate ablations, were not separately recorded where they repeat the same acquisition/extrapolation comparisons already represented in R3–R12. Their text describes rankings as broadly preserved across surrogate substitutions and data splits.

untested.parts: No fitted exponents. No separate N, D and C axes with the others non-bottlenecked. Only a qualitative fit within about 3–4 orders of magnitude of FLOPs on surrogate frontiers.
Extrapolation spans only 10–20×Cmax (about 1.3 orders of magnitude), not several orders. Targets are surrogate predictions, not new large runs.
Only N* prediction is scored. D*, exponent stability, and the Kaplan-vs-Hoffmann split are not reported.
Depth, width and heads are varied, but loss at fixed N versus shape is not analysed.
Only CLIP contrastive pretraining. No image-only, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer results.
Downstream tasks are explicitly excluded, though the surrogates support them.
Training schedule, data and curve bending are not varied or tested. Compute counting enters only via the 6ND failure on CLIP.

missing.what: Loss-extrapolation regret for all four acquisitions under Kaplan and Chinchilla3. Text: Chinchilla3 is better on OpenCLIP across all acquisitions, with comparable regret on LLM.

Interaction summary: Chinchilla3 is said to 'consistently outperform' for loss but is brittle for N* due to identifiability. Power-law N* is also said to be ineffective for RS, which conflicts with the Fig 6 text ('except CARBS').
Surrogate ablations (XGBoost surrogate, disjoint data splits) preserving rankings; needed to judge whether conclusions are surrogate artefacts.

record.verdict_notes: All 'empirical' targets are TabPFN surrogate predictions, so verdicts are conditional on surrogate fidelity (LLM R² 0.77). Extrapolation spans only 20×. Nearly all evidence is figure-only. Internal inconsistencies: Table 4 RS LLM values are not monotonic; Fig 6 vs Fig 15 disagree on RS; R6 vs the 'consistently outperforms' claim. The reader's V7 label on R17–R20 is dropped because those rows are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares loss extrapolation fits, but does not report fitted exponents or separately establish power-law relationships along parameters, tokens, and compute when the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
The target is 20×Cmax, not several orders of magnitude above the acquired runs. Some reported full-configuration evaluations give achieved loss rather than a direct forecast of held-out loss.

The study evaluates predictions of optimal model size and full configurations, but does not establish whether both optimal parameter count and token count follow stable powers of compute, or compare whether parameters grow faster than data versus equally.
The study includes one vision-language training pipeline, but does not test image-only or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

The study shows acquisition strategy and benchmark family affect extrapolation outcomes. It does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting procedure to estimate their effects on exponents, and does not test whether curves bend away from a single power law.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is broadly accurate. Figure 4's LLM discussion favors Kaplan, whereas the later Figure 14 discussion claims consistent Chinchilla3 superiority; results use surrogates, 10 seeds except Figure 2's selected seed, and substantially smaller scales than current frontier models.

statements.correction: Target: 20×Cmax. OpenCLIP: 2M–357M parameters. LLM: 16M–1B parameters. Chinchilla3 N* prediction fails on OpenCLIP under the retained 6ND heuristic. Empirical-power-law N* prediction is poor under CARBS. CARBS with Chinchilla3 has the lowest final N* regret. No demonstrated breakdown of the underlying stable allocation powers.
statements.problem: The reported prediction failures and conditions are accurate, but the limits_scope placement treats estimation failures as evidence that the underlying compute-optimal allocation law needs qualification.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: tested LLM and OpenCLIP loss extrapolations
reader_labels.reason: Loss prediction depends on both the fitting method and acquisition strategy: Chinchilla Approach 3 is closer in some conditions, while Kaplan is more reliable in others (R3–R6); the paper does not report exponents or isolate the three scaling axes.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: full-parameter extrapolation at 0.1× and 0.5×Ctarget search budgets
reader_labels.reason: Achieved losses at predicted configurations remain above the best empirical loss, with especially large gaps for OpenCLIP; the LLM RS result at 0.5× is also worse than at 0.1× (R13–R20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Power-law model-size predictions depend on acquisition strategy and method: CARBS performs poorly with the empirical power-law fit but is reported as best with Chinchilla Approach 3 (R7–R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: optimal model-size prediction in LLM and OpenCLIP benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The ability to predict N* varies with architecture family, acquisition strategy, and extrapolation method; the study does not establish a stable joint parameter-and-token allocation power law (R7–R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The tested VLM results are method- and acquisition-dependent, including a failure attributed to the Chinchilla compute heuristic and poor full-configuration losses, so they do not establish a modality-general power-law form (R3, R5, R7, R15, R16, R19, R20).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: acquisition and extrapolation choices tested across LLM and OpenCLIP benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Reported prediction quality and method rankings change with acquisition strategy, benchmark family, and extrapolation method (R3–R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: full-parameter extrapolation at the two tested search budgets
reader_labels.reason: Full-configuration performance is imperfect and does not uniformly improve with more search budget: LLM RS loss is 1.71 at 0.1× and 1.89 at 0.5×Ctarget (R17–R20).
